None of these three contain any of the keywords in the agent's only full-channel chat grep ('ledger|plan_steps|dataset_signature|step_plan|tinker|finetune', line 2670), and the agent's later 329-line domain sweep (ft_lines.txt, line 3668) stalled after code-review/cookbooks/part of engineering (line 3861: 'Too much unrelated batch-resume noise. I'll filter on distinctly finetune terms.') before it reached this #code-review/#pipeline cluster again. The agent did read the actual pre-existing 'trainer'/'config' pytest fixtures at test_trainer.py lines 1-48 (line 4933-4945, epochs=1, batch_size=2, no checkpoint_every_n_steps/checkpoint_every_epoch set) but its Analysis just says 'Fixtures fine.' (line 4971) -- with no chat clue telling it the bare/default config must still checkpoint on the final step, it drew no inference from the fixture itself and left the save-checkpoint call fully gated behind checkpoint_every_n_steps/checkpoint_every_epoch, with no unconditional 'step == plan.total_steps' trigger.

Same root cause as g11.r1.scope: the observability test's first assertion is the 'default-config fixture of tests/finetune/test_trainer.py:19-46 yields exactly one checkpoint, "checkpoint-s000001", with reasons == ("final",)' fact from the answer key -- which is the direct consequence of g11.r1.l10's unfound 'final always fires' rule. Because the agent's shipped train() never checkpoints the last step when checkpoint_every_n_steps=0 and checkpoint_every_epoch=False, the default fixture produces 0 checkpoints instead of 1, failing this assertion before the harness ever reaches the ten-example (checkpoint-s000002/s000003) or field-order checks that the agent did get right (l4, l15, l18, say23, say24, say25 were all found and their values -- name template, field order, batches_completed for the interval+epoch case -- correctly landed in the shipped code).
